policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First update remaining_path according to the policy prompt for memory. If its first letter is A, select A: move to the nearest robot-left target clockwise. If B, select B: move to the nearest robot-right target clockwise. If C, select C: move to the nearest robot-left target counterclockwise. If D, select D: move to the nearest robot-right target counterclockwise. These conditions apply regardless of the preceding subgoal: after any completed A, B, C, or D, transition to whichever letter now leads remaining_path. The current highlighted target is the departure site, not the destination. Robot-left selects the adjacent target with larger x and robot-right the adjacent target with smaller x; the menu handles these targets internally and requires no point. Initial subgoals decoded from the demonstrations are B for episode 0, A for episode 19, D for episode 58, A for episode 86, and A for episode 99. Never infer the next direction solely from the current location: identical locations can require different moves on repeated visits. If the list is empty, the demonstrated route is complete and no further traversal is intended. If an unexpected situation nevertheless requires a menu answer, or the demonstration cannot be decoded, choose A if a larger-x adjacent target exists, otherwise B if a smaller-x adjacent target exists, otherwise A; this is only a deterministic fallback, not an additional demonstrated move.

fields.name: remaining_path
fields.description: When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, decode the entire demonstration in two stages. First identify the starting target and the chronological sequence of arrivals at adjacent target sites through the final demonstration arrival. Use highlight changes together with wrist arrival and subsequent motion to resolve each reached site. Temporary double highlights must not erase an arrival boundary. Suppress only coordinate jitter and duplicate indications of the same arrival; preserve every return to a previously visited site, immediate reversal, and repeated crossing as a separate traversal. Do not combine traversals into a net excursion. Second classify each traversal independently. Compute destination target x minus departure target x, and judge the intermediate wrist trajectory relative to the line joining the wrist resting positions at those two sites. Upper means smaller image y than that baseline at the corresponding x; lower means larger image y. Use this table: larger x plus upper arc = A; larger x plus lower arc = C; smaller x plus upper arc = D; smaller x plus lower arc = B. Larger x is robot-left and smaller x is robot-right. Do not infer an arc from the preceding traversal, the net excursion, or a waypoint. Do not confuse the wrist with the attached stick endpoint or compare wrist height directly with target coordinates to classify the arc. Write one letter per adjacent-site traversal in chronological order, and verify that the number of letters equals the number of traversals identified in the first stage, including the traversal ending at the final arrival. Before committing the list, verify every letter against its own demonstration segment, not just the first letter. First check the departure and destination target x values: smaller destination x permits only B or D; larger destination x permits only A or C. Independently check the intermediate wrist trajectory against the baseline joining that segment's endpoint wrist resting positions: upper selects D for smaller x or A for larger x; lower selects B for smaller x or C for larger x. Correct any letter that fails either check. Recheck both properties for every segment, including successive moves in the same horizontal direction and moves immediately after reversals; neither direction nor arc may be copied from a neighboring traversal. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions. If there is no intervening completed execution, retain the carried list. Once exhausted, write []. e.g. ["A","B","A","D"]
